newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn mulls use of Bundesbank gold-govt sources.
newsitem.headline: Bonn mulls use of Bundesbank gold-govt sources.

text.p: German government sources said on Wednesday that the government was considering using Bundesbank gold reserves for budgetary purposes, confirming details of a German newspaper report.
The sources added however that the gold reserves would not be used to cover budget shortfalls but to finance investments.
The sources gave no further details.

According to an advance copy of a report to appear in Thursday's "Handelsblatt" newspaper, the Bundesbank owns around 95 million ounces of fine gold valued on average at 144 marks per ounce, for a total of 13.7 billion marks.
A reevaluation at current market prices of 600 marks per ounce would bring the gold's total worth up to 57 billion marks, creating some 40 billion marks of extra value, it said.
The newspaper added the additional reserves created by such a reevaluation could at least in part be used for budgetary purposes.
Such a move was particularly being urged by the FDP junior government coalition partners to avoid the risk of tax increases, it said.

Earlier, government coalition sources said a key tax estimate due on Thursday would show that 1997 tax revenues would be nearly 20 billion marks less than expected, casting doubts over Bonn's ability to meet the budget deficit criterion laid out for entry into the single European currency in 1999.
